fatal_errors: The proposed heat treatment does not reconstruct the target intervention of Zr alloying at x = 0.01, 0.05, and 0.1.
The cited precipitation evidence concerns Al0.7CoCrFeNi rather than AlCoCrFeNi2.1, so formation of the same L12 population under the proposed aging schedule is not established.
Neither cited source supports improved chloride corrosion resistance, room-temperature creep resistance, or operation up to approximately 700 °C.
The proposed universal improvement misses the target composition-dependent tradeoff: x = 0.05 maximizes mechanical and creep performance, whereas x = 0.1 maximizes corrosion resistance.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested strength, creep, thermal-stability, and corrosion concerns with a single testable intervention, and low-temperature precipitation strengthening is credible in a related lamellar eutectic HEA. It is nevertheless a different intervention from the hidden target and lacks direct evidence that AlCoCrFeNi2.1 will form the proposed coherent L12 precipitates after 600–650 °C aging. The corrosion claim is particularly speculative because preserving microstructural uniformity does not by itself demonstrate formation of a protective passive film in chloride solution. The asserted room-temperature-to-700 °C service boundary is also unsupported by the cited studies. The factorial aging experiment could distinguish precipitation and mechanical effects, but it needs an unaged, identically processed control, quantitative creep and corrosion thresholds, and a rule that rejects the intervention if ductility or corrosion deteriorates even when strength rises.
